### poiseuille2d {#sec-example-laminar-poiseuille2d}

For basic tests of boundary conditions, a comparison with analytical solutions is the easiest and most accurate approach.
One of the fundamental applications of fluid dynamics is that of laminar flow of a Newtonian fluid in a circular pipe.
This is known as Poiseuille flow.
The analytical solution is easily found and is therefore a common benchmark case.
It is also one of the first examples in most fluid dynamics textbooks for the application of the principles of fluid dynamics.
The extension of the Poiseuille flow in a round pipe from 2D to 3D is trivial; consequently, it is also an ideal test case for curved boundaries in 3D as well.

#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I \subseteq [0, 2] \times [0, 1] \times \R_{\geq 0}$ is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^2$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid with kinematic viscosity $\nu \in \R_{> 0}$ and constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= -\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p + \nu \Delta \vel \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I.
\end{align}
In a straight channel of height $H$ and length $L$, the steady solution is the Poiseuille flow
\begin{align}
    u_\text{P}(y) &= \frac{4\, u_\text{max}\, y (H - y)}{H^2}, \\
    p_\text{P}(x) &= p_0 \left(1 - \frac{x}{L}\right), \quad p_0 = \frac{8 \rho \nu u_\text{max} L}{H^2},
\end{align}
with $\vel = (u_\text{P}(y), 0)^\top$, against which the example measures its error.

#### Boundary conditions

The boundary $\partial \Omega = \Gamma_D \cup \Gamma_\text{out} \cup \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ consists of three parts (@fig-poiseuille2d-domain): the inlet $\Gamma_D$ on the left, where the Poiseuille profile is prescribed as a Dirichlet condition, the outlet $\Gamma_\text{out}$ on the right, where the pressure is prescribed, and the two channel walls $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$,
\begin{align}
    \vel &= (u_\text{P}(y), 0)^\top \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_D \times \I, \\
    p &= p_\text{P}(L) \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_\text{out} \times \I, \\
    \vel &= \mathbf{0} \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}} \times \I.
\end{align}
The simulation starts from the analytical solution, $\vel = (u_\text{P}(y), 0)^\top$ and $p = p_\text{P}(x)$ in $\Omega$ at $t = 0$, and relaxes to the steady state of the discrete scheme.

#### Domain

The channel has the length $L = 2\,\mathrm{m}$ and the height $H = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ (@fig-poiseuille2d-domain).
With the maximum velocity $u_\text{max} = 1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $\nu = 0.1\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$, the Reynolds number is $Re = u_\text{max} H / \nu = 10$.
`prepareGeometry()` assigns the material numbers (MN) shown in @fig-poiseuille2d-domain.

![Domain and boundary conditions of `poiseuille2d` in its default configuration, with the material numbers (MN) assigned in `prepareGeometry()`.](/examples/laminar/poiseuille2d/doc/fig/poiseuille2dDomain.svg){width="80%" #fig-poiseuille2d-domain .lightbox}

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid with the lattice spacing $\Delta x = H / N$, where $N = 50$ cells resolve the height of the channel.

The LBM collision operator is the BGK operator with a single relaxation time ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), used as `BGKdynamics`, together with the D2Q9 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)).
In the default configuration, the walls (MN 2) and the inlet (MN 3) are treated with `InterpolatedVelocity` and the outlet (MN 4) with `InterpolatedPressure` ([Define Boundary Method](/content/06_initial_boundary.qmd#sec-defineBoundaryMethod)).

The example is meant for comparing boundary conditions and flow setups, which are selected in `main()`:

- `BOUNDARY_TYPE` chooses the wall boundary: `bounceBack`, `local` (`LocalVelocity`, with `LocalVelocity` and `LocalPressure` at the inlet and outlet), `interpolated` (default), `freeSlip` or `partialSlip`, where `TUNER_PARAM` blends between no-slip and free slip. The error norms are only computed for the no-slip boundaries.
- `FLOW_TYPE` chooses between `nonForced` (default), the setup described above, and `forced`, where the channel is periodic in $x$ and a constant body force $F = p_0 / L$ drives the flow instead of the inlet and outlet. The forced setup uses `ForcedBGKdynamics`.
- Compiling with `ENABLE_MRT` defined replaces the BGK operator by the multiple relaxation time operator, `MRTdynamics` and `ForcedMRTdynamics`.

The corresponding lattice is defined inside the case definition in `case.h` as in @lst-poiseuille2d-case.

::: {#lst-poiseuille2d-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<
  NavierStokes, Lattice<FLOATING_POINT_TYPE, descriptors::D2Q9<FORCE>>
>;
```
Case definition for the `poiseuille2d` example. The `FORCE` field holds the body force of the forced setup.
:::

The parameters for the simulation are set in `main()` and given in @tbl-poiseuille2d-params.
The unit converter `UnitConverterFromResolutionAndRelaxationTime` derives the time step size from the resolution and the lattice relaxation time.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | $N$ | $50$ | cells per channel height $H$ |
| `DOMAIN_EXTENT` | $L \times H$ | $2\,\mathrm{m} \times 1\,\mathrm{m}$ | length and height of the channel |
| `PHYS_CHAR_VELOCITY` | $u_\text{max}$ | $1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ | maximum velocity of the Poiseuille profile |
| `REYNOLDS` | $Re$ | $10$ | Reynolds number $u_\text{max} H / \nu$, which sets $\nu = 0.1\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$ |
| `LATTICE_RELAXATION_TIME` | $\tau$ | $0.8$ | lattice relaxation time |
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | $T$ | $30\,\mathrm{s}$ | upper limit of the simulated time, $75\,000$ time steps |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DENSITY` | $\rho$ | $1\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ | density |
| `TUNER_PARAM` | | $0.5$ | blending of the partial slip boundary, from $0$ (no-slip) to $1$ (free slip) |
| `FLOW_TYPE` | | `nonForced` | inlet and outlet (`nonForced`) or periodic with body force (`forced`) |
| `BOUNDARY_TYPE` | | `interpolated` | boundary condition at the walls |
| `CONVERGENCE_PRECISION` | | $10^{-9}$ | bound for the relative standard deviation of the average energy |
| `CONV_ITER` | | $0.25\,\mathrm{s}$ | time window of the convergence check |
| `VTK_ENABLED` | | `true` | write VTK output and heat maps |
| `GNUPLOT_ENABLED` | | `true` | plot the velocity profile at the last time step, with `EOC` the errors over the resolution |
| `COMPUTE_ERROR` | | `true` | compute the error norms at every statistics output |
| `EOC` | | `false` | convergence study over $N = 30, 50, 70, 100$ instead of a single run |
| `PHYS_VTK_ITER_T` | | $T/20 = 1.5\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the VTK output |
| `PHYS_STAT_ITER_T` | | $T/20 = 1.5\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the console statistics and the error norms |

: Parameters of `poiseuille2d`, as set in `main()`. {#tbl-poiseuille2d-params}

#### Validation

The simulation stops as soon as the relative standard deviation of the average energy over the last $0.25\,\mathrm{s}$ falls below $10^{-9}$, which happens after $46\,600$ time steps at $t = 18.6\,\mathrm{s}$.
At every statistics output and at the end, `errorNorms()` prints the absolute and relative $L^1$, $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ errors of the velocity, the strain rate and the pressure against the analytical solution, over the fluid cells (MN 1).
The VTK output contains the analytical velocity next to the simulated one.

@fig-poiseuille2d-profile compares the velocity profile at $x = L/2$ with the analytical solution, and @tbl-poiseuille2d-errors lists the relative $L^2$ errors for the default resolution and for $N = 100$, run with `--RESOLUTION 100`.
Halving the lattice spacing reduces all three errors by a factor of about four, which is the second order convergence of the scheme.

![Velocity profile of `poiseuille2d` at $x = L/2$ at the end of the simulation with $N = 50$, compared with the analytical Poiseuille profile.](/examples/laminar/poiseuille2d/doc/fig/profile/profile.svg){width="60%" #fig-poiseuille2d-profile .lightbox}

| Resolution $N$ | velocity | strain rate | pressure |
|---|---|---|---|
| $50$ (default) | $1.15 \cdot 10^{-3}$ | $1.49 \cdot 10^{-3}$ | $3.01 \cdot 10^{-3}$ |
| $100$ | $2.87 \cdot 10^{-4}$ | $3.78 \cdot 10^{-4}$ | $7.54 \cdot 10^{-4}$ |

: Relative $L^2$ errors of `poiseuille2d` at the end of the simulation. {#tbl-poiseuille2d-errors}

With `--EOC 1`, `main()` runs the simulation for the resolutions $N = 30$, $50$, $70$ and $100$ one after the other, without VTK output.
At the end of each run, `getResults()` adds the absolute errors to `tmp/gnuplotData/error.png`, which plots them over the resolution on logarithmic axes together with a linear fit (@fig-poiseuille2d-error).
The fitted slopes are about $-2$ for the velocity and for the $L^1$ and $L^2$ errors of the strain rate and the pressure, which confirms the second order convergence.
The $L^\infty$ errors of the strain rate and the pressure converge more slowly, with the slopes $-1.2$ and $-1.7$.
At $N = 25$ and $N = 40$, the mean density grows during the run and the pressure error does not converge, which is why the study uses other resolutions.

![Absolute $L^1$, $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ errors of the velocity, the strain rate and the pressure of `poiseuille2d` over the resolution $N$, with linear fits on logarithmic axes, written by the example with `--EOC 1`. The legend gives the slopes of the fits.](/examples/laminar/poiseuille2d/doc/fig/error/error.png){width="80%" #fig-poiseuille2d-error .lightbox}

#### Files

```
poiseuille2d/
├── poiseuille2d.cpp   main(): parameters, one run or the convergence study; run(): mesh, geometry, lattice, initial values and time loop
├── case.h             Case type, flow and boundary variants, error norms and output
└── Makefile
```

The results are written to `tmp/` in the directory the example is run from: `vtkData/poiseuille2d.pvd` opens all time steps in ParaView, `imageData/` holds the velocity heat maps and `gnuplotData/` the velocity profile of the last time step, or with `EOC` the error plot. The heat maps and plots are drawn with gnuplot; without it, only the data in `gnuplotData/data/` is written.
